summary: Modular monolith: React + Vite (SPA), Go (net/http + chi), PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) database on Google Cloud Run. It matches the team's languages and is estimated at $1,400-$2,400 per month.

architecture.name: modular monolith
architecture.justification: One deployable with clear internal modules per feature area suits a team of 5 and 4 feature areas (payments, realtime, file storage, multi-tenancy): simple to run now, with seams to split later if load demands it.

alternatives.why_not: Adds service boundaries, network calls and per-service deployment that this team does not need at this scale (team 5).
With 4 feature areas, code without module boundaries tends to tangle as the team grows.
Per-request functions suit light, spiky work; this backend runs as a long-lived service on Google Cloud Run, which suits websockets, background jobs and steady traffic better.

frontend.justification: React + Vite (SPA) matches the team's typescript skills; offloads rendering to clients, scales on a CDN; is a proven choice for realtime collab projects.

alternatives.why_not: Angular scores 0.3 points lower overall, mainly on coverage of the required features (0.6 points).
Nuxt scores 0.4 points lower overall, mainly on coverage of the required features (0.6 points).

tradeoffs: Poor SEO without prerendering
Slow first load on weak devices

backend.justification: Go (net/http + chi) matches the team's go skills; handles many concurrent realtime connections well; compiled, low latency; is a proven choice for realtime collab projects.

alternatives.why_not: Node.js + NestJS scores 2.0 points lower overall, mainly on performance (1.5 points) and scalability (0.8 points).
C# + ASP.NET Core scores 2.7 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.2 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.6 points).

tradeoffs: No batteries, more code per feature

database.choice: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL in Belgium (europe-west1)
database.justification: PostgreSQL gives ACID transactions for money-handling data; can be placed in Belgium (europe-west1), an EU region, which keeps GDPR transfers simple; excellent query planner, rich indexing. It runs as Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, the managed service on the same cloud as the application, so backups, patching and failover are the provider's job.

alternatives.why_not: MySQL (managed or self-hosted) is a close second: only 1.2 points behind, with no single weakness.
Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL scores 2.8 points lower overall, mainly on vendor lock-in (1.0 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.9 points).

tradeoffs: Write scaling beyond one primary needs design

hosting.justification: Google Cloud Run can be placed in Belgium (europe-west1), an EU region, which keeps GDPR transfers simple; offers a 99.95% SLA, in line with the 99.9% target; autoscale to many instances; is a proven choice for realtime collab projects.

alternatives.why_not: Fly.io scores 0.9 points lower overall, mainly on maintainability (0.4 points) and scalability (0.4 points).
Azure Container Apps is a close second: only 1.4 points behind, with no single weakness.

tradeoffs: GCP only

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 500 requests/second and about 140M requests/month from 50K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.9% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.

warnings.message: Use a hosted checkout from a PCI DSS certified provider so card data never reaches your servers.

GDPR: keep a record of processing, sign a data processing agreement with every vendor that handles personal data, support access and erasure requests, and use standard contractual clauses for any transfer outside the EU/EEA; consider EU data residency to keep transfers simple.

A p95 of 100 ms with live updates for users spread across regions is reachable only over persistent connections (WebSockets) to servers in the users' region; avoid cold-starting functions on the hot path and load-test the fan-out at the expected 5,000 concurrent users.

Expected cost ($1,400-$2,400) has its midpoint above the $1,500 budget; the low end fits. The largest items are hosting (Google Cloud Run, $670-$1,000) and database (PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted), $540-$1,000), so start there: trim optional services, cap usage, or accept a tighter margin.

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
